resources.string: Safe Area adds colored guides to help you frame your videos. The guides stay on your screen and do not appear in the recording.

Tap Calibrate now, choose your camera from the list, then select Video mode in portrait, 9:16. The mask and arrows will appear over the camera.

Use ↑ and ↓ to move the mask. Hold an arrow to keep moving; release to stop. Tap the green Done button to return here. Your position is saved and the arrows are hidden. You can also skip this step.

To show the SAFE button and guides over your camera, Android needs your permission.

1. On the next screen, choose %1$s if a list appears.
2. Turn on Allow display over other apps (the name can vary).
3. Use Back to return to Safe Area.

Once permission is granted, you can use Show quick button. This does not turn on camera detection.
This settings screen could not be opened. Open Android Settings and find Safe Area under Apps.

What to do on the next screen:
1. Find %1$s. It may be under Installed apps or Downloaded apps.
2. Turn it on and confirm Android’s message if you agree.
3. Use Back to return to Safe Area. The app will check whether it is enabled.

If Android blocks the switch, return here and tap Activation blocked? Menu names vary by phone.

If Android says Restricted settings, or the switch is blocked:

1. Open App info below for %1$s.
2. If available, open the ⋮ menu and choose Allow restricted settings. Only do this if you trust the app you installed.
3. Return to Safe Area and try Enable camera detection again.

This can happen with APK installs. Menu names vary. If the option is missing, check your phone’s help. You can still use the button manually.
Choose the app you use to record videos. Safe Area will follow this app. You can change it later in Automatic opening.
No camera or other app could be listed. Check that your camera app is installed and enabled, then try again. You can still use Show quick button manually.
Permission is still off. Tap Show quick button to see the steps again.

Safe Area uses Android AccessibilityService to detect when you open or leave the camera app you select, so it can show or hide the floating button and guides.

If you also enable experimental Video-only mode, it reads that camera’s accessible controls locally to distinguish Photo from Video. It does not capture screenshots, save control text or send it to anyone.

This feature is optional. You can use the guides manually without enabling accessibility, and turn off the service at any time in Android settings.

Tap Continue to consent to this use and open Android accessibility settings. You will choose whether to enable the Safe Area service there.
Show the mask only in \"Video\" mode

The mask is only needed when recording videos.
It can therefore disappear when the camera switches to Photo mode.

It uses Android accessibility features: the camera app exposes its active mode and Safe Area detects it to turn the mask on / off.

Currently supported automatic profiles:
• Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (SM-S948B), Android 17 / API 37, Samsung Camera 17.0.00.43: portrait, in Italian, English, French, Spanish and German.
• Google Pixel 2 XL, Android 11 / API 30, Google Camera 8.2.204.362396359.12: portrait, camera languages Italian, English, French, Spanish and German.
Other configurations use manual control.

If you are a developer, you can contribute by adding profiles on GitHub.

Created by Marco Rinaldi, creator of Pistacchissimo
A lightweight, independent composition guide for your Android camera. Tested on Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra.
Social Safe Area grew out of my own needs when filming content for Pistacchissimo. I chose to make it free and open source to share it with the community.
